children: will be reporting earnings this Monday after the bell. Here’s what to look for.

Semtech beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $341.9 million, up 32.7% year on year. It was an impressive quarter for the company, with a significant improvement in its inventory levels and a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Semtech a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Semtech’s revenue to grow 56% year on year, improving from the 12.7% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Semtech rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at Semtech’s peers in the semiconductor manufacturing segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Entegris delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 24.6%, beating analysts’ expectations by 8.6%, and Kulicke and Soffa reported revenues up 131%, topping estimates by 8.6%. Entegris traded down 3.1% following the results while Kulicke and Soffa was also down 8.1%.

Over the past year, investors have repeatedly shifted their focus from one macro narrative to another (AI disruption and AI capex spending to geopolitics, interest rates, and the broader health of the economy). Unfortunately, semiconductor manufacturing stocks have struggled in this environment as share prices are down 17.5% on average over the last month. Semtech is down 31.4% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $203.80 (compared to the current share price of $90.51).
ALSO WORTH WATCHING: Nvidia’s Quiet Partner.
Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.

title: What to expect from Semtech’s Q3 earnings
